Set up the sum of $3N$ terms: $S_{3N} = \frac{3N}{2}[2a + 2(3N - 1)] = 5760 \implies N(a + 3N - 1) = 1920$.
Substitute $a = 57 - 2N$ to form $N^2 + 56N - 1920 = 0$, solve for positive integer $N = 24$, and find $a = 9$.
walkthrough:
Express the $N$-th term in terms of $a$ and $N$ with $d = 2$:
$$u_N = a + (N - 1)(2) = 55 \implies a + 2N - 2 = 55 \implies a = 57 - 2N$$

Set up the equation for the sum of the first $3N$ terms ($S_{3N} = 5760$):
$$S_{3N} = \frac{3N}{2}\left[2a + (3N - 1)(2)\right] = 3N(a + 3N - 1) = 5760 \implies N(a + 3N - 1) = 1920$$

Substitute $a = 57 - 2N$ to form a quadratic equation in $N$:
$$N\left((57 - 2N) + 3N - 1\right) = 1920 \implies N(N + 56) = 1920 \implies N^2 + 56N - 1920 = 0$$

Factorise and solve for the positive integer $N$:
$$(N - 24)(N + 80) = 0 \implies N = 24 \quad (\text{rejecting } N = -80)$$
